business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tailoring of Licensed Theatrical Costume Robes and Synthetic Wigs

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction with a single company-law and tax-law regime; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; Romano-Germanic doctrine, with EU law supremacy incorporated)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU, consolidated 2016) — intra-EU establishment and capital-movement freedoms

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-51 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF) as amended by LOI n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II) and Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 19 février 2020, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); Article L. 561-2-2 CMF defining the 'bénéficiaire effectif' (UBO) at the 25% direct/indirect capital or voting-rights threshold; Articles L. 561-45 et seq. CMF and Décret n° 2016-567 du 10 mai 2016 establishing the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) filed at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI; Article L. 561-15 CMF imposing suspicious-transaction reporting to TRACFIN (French Financial Intelligence Unit); LOI n° 2019-486 du 22 mai 2019 (PACTE) eliminating the minimum capital requirement for SAS; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675 (high-risk third countries).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the valid national identity document or passport of each SAS shareholder and UBO (KYC appraisal sheet)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or competent civil-registry authority of the holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for a state party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) or Consular Legalization through the French Embassy or Consulate in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / company-registry extract (extrait du registre ou équivalent) of each non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with sworn French translation annexed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of all non-French constitutive documents, identity evidence and address proof
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator registered as an expert judiciaire before a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the underlying source public document to which the sworn translation is attached

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility invoice or regulated-bank statement dated within the last three months) of the SAS President and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local public-utility supplier or regulated credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization where the document is not a notarized public deed, or certified translation of an apostilled notarized attestation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the SAS President, directors, shareholders and all identified UBOs against: (i) the French national asset-freezing regime (Décret n° 2019-250 du 27 mars 2019 on freezing assets, including the Banque de France register of frozen accounts); (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, including Regulation (EU) n° 269/2014 (Ukrainian territorial integrity) and Regulation (EU) n° 1267/1999 as amended (UN-derived Al-Qaida/Taliban/ISIL lists); (iii) the UN Consolidated List (Security Council resolutions 1267, 1988, 1718 and associated resolutions); (iv) the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists as best-practice screening given USD settlement rails through Stripe and Shopify Payments; (v) FATF public statements and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675 high-risk-jurisdiction classifications; and (vi) politically exposed person (PEP) identification, including family members and close associates, under Article L. 561-10 CMF. The AML/KYC file must be refreshed at each change of shareholders or UBOs and retained for five years after termination of the business relationship (Article L. 561-6 CMF); any suspicion must be reported to TRACFIN under Article L. 561-15 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), the single digital filing portal operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), transmitting incorporation filings to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, with name-availability verification against the INPI data / RNCS (Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés) database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article L. 210-1 of the Code de commerce, the dénomination sociale (corporate name) may be freely selected, provided it is lawful, non-deceptive and sufficiently distinctive. All filings on the Guichet Unique must be completed in the French language. The corporate name must be entered in standard Latin characters; any non-Latin script must be transliterated (romanized) into Latin characters. Where a foreign-language element is used, a French translation or transliteration may be recorded in the statuts for the benefit of French commercial counterparties, and the registered Latin-script name is the authoritative form for the RCS and the EU Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Crédit — regulated banking and credit terms requiring prior authorization from the ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority)
Assurance, Insurance, Mutuelle — regulated insurance and mutual-assurance terms requiring prior ACPR authorization
Avocat, Barreau, Notaire, Huissier, Commissaire de Justice — reserved legal-profession designations
Médecin, Pharmacie, Clinique, Hôpital, Cabinet Médical — reserved health-profession and healthcare-establishment designations
France, République, National, Officiel, Gouvernemental — sovereignty tokens implying state sponsorship or official endorsement
Armée, Marine Nationale, Gendarmerie, Police, Sécurité Nationale — national-defense and public-order tokens
Société Anonyme, SA, SARL, SNC, EURL — legal-form tokens that may not misrepresent the actual SAS corporate form
Chambre de Commerce, Commune, Mairie, Ministère, Préfecture — public-institutional denominations
Expert-Comptable, Commissaire aux Comptes, CAC — reserved accounting and statutory-audit professional titles
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not issue a statutory name-reservation certificate; availability is verified at filing time through the Guichet Unique and the INPI/RNCS databases, with a de facto re-check and internal-hold window of approximately 30 days before formal submission. If the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce refuses the proposed dénomination sociale (on grounds of identity, confusing similarity with an existing registered name or trademark in the same activity, or violation of public order or prohibited-token rules), the applicant may: (1) submit a revised name within the same Guichet Unique file at no additional administrative fee; (2) within 15 days of the refusal, file with the Greffe a written, reasoned application for re-examination, annexing distinctiveness arguments and, where relevant, written coexistence consent from the prior rights-holder; (3) if the Greffe maintains the refusal, petition the judge responsible for surveillance of the registry (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) in summary proceedings (référé) for an order directing registration; (4) within one month of the judicial decision, lodge an appeal with the competent Cour d'appel; and (5) where the conflict arises from a confusingly similar trademark, seek cancellation or revocation of the conflicting mark, or obtain a dedicated coexistence agreement, before re-filing. The final registered name is evidenced by the RCS extract issued through the Guichet Unique, and clerical-correction requests are accepted within 15 days of issuance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with material caveats: the SAS's siège social may be established at the premises of an approved domiciliation provider under Article L. 123-11-3 of the Code de commerce and its implementing decrees, provided a documented 12-month minimum domiciliation agreement, continuous physical right of occupancy, and legal-service forwarding are in place. Because ISIC 3240 comprises the actual tailoring of licensed theatrical costume robes and synthetic wigs, the acquiring bank, the Payment Service Providers (Stripe and Shopify Payments), and the French tax administration may require a physical operating unit to evidence genuine commercial substance; a virtual office is acceptable for the initial 12-month administrative/registered-address phase if manufacturing is outsourced, no inventory is stored at the domiciliation address, and the domiciliation provider is duly authorized to receive legal process. If the SAS later hires employees, stores finished goods in France, or opens a production workshop, a separate tangible establishment (établissement) must be registered with the URSSAF and the relevant business-tax filings must be updated.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ≈15–20% within the first 24 months for a virtual-office SAS with no employees, fully outsourced manufacturing, and no inventory on French territory; the risk rises to ≈45–60% if the SAS occupies physical premises, employs personnel (unannounced URSSAF and Labour Inspectorate visits), or warehouses cosplay stock in France (DGCCRF consumer-safety inspections, public-health product checks, and customs origin-controls). For this low-risk e-commerce retail profile with Stripe and Shopify Payments, the near-term supervisory scrutiny is principally merchant-underwriting and payment-monitoring by the Payment Service Providers rather than French administrative on-site raids.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated statutory tariff per 100-character block of the announcement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) — identification, documentation, and electronic filing of the RBE sheet
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (filing) / licensed compliance service provider (preparation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator registered as expert judiciaire before a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — €70 to €120 per certified page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing business registration; Articles R.123-1 et seq. governing registration formalities and the national business register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration data transmitted to the competent Greffe du tribunal de commerce and the Registre national des entreprises (RNE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online declaration of creation of a legal entity (déclaration de création d'une personne morale) submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, accompanied by the signed SAS articles of association and beneficial-owner declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies; capital may be set at EUR 1 or any higher amount. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked account and evidenced by a certificate of deposit. Contributions in kind are generally fully contributed upon issuance, subject to statutory valuation rules and possible auditor exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the Company accept and record the subscription by the shareholders for the entire issued share capital in accordance with the signed articles of association and the applicable deposit certificate. Resolved that the registered office be established at [full French address], effective from incorporation. Resolved that [name] be appointed President (Président) for the term and powers specified in the articles, and that [name] be appointed Director-General (Directeur Général), if applicable. The officers are authorized to complete all registration, banking, tax, employment, insurance, and licensing formalities. The resolution is approved and entered in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm SAS structure, corporate purpose, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for filing; competent commercial court registry for registration jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the SAS form, define the corporate purpose to cover manufacture, design, purchase, sale, import, export, and online retail of costumes, accessories, props, and synthetic wigs, and secure a French registered office. Obtain a domiciliation agreement, commercial lease, or proof of premises. Ensure the proposed activity does not accidentally include regulated professions or protected third-party intellectual property.
required_dossiers: Identity and address evidence for shareholders and officers
Foreign corporate shareholder registration extract and representative authority, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the corporate purpose, address, identity data, or supporting evidence before submission; obtain a registry pre-check from the competent Greffe where the activity description is unusually broad or premises-based.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute articles and appoint corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company shareholders and designated corporate officers; INPI Guichet unique for subsequent filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles of association electronically or in wet ink. State the share capital, share classes, subscription allocation, transfer restrictions, decision rules, accounting year, President appointment mechanism, and any Directeur Général appointment. French law does not require notarization of SAS articles in ordinary cases. Notarial execution is required only for transactions requiring a notarial deed, such as certain real-estate contributions.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment decisions or appointment provisions in the articles
Declarations of non-conviction and parentage for individual officers
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-execute defective signatures, correct inconsistent dates or capital allocations, and replace incomplete officer declarations. Foreign-language documents should be accompanied by a French translation where requested by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital and obtain bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or authorized deposit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account in the name of the company being formed. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions, obtain the certificate of deposit of funds, and retain the blocked-account evidence for the INPI filing. The account is released or converted after registration and presentation of the Kbis or equivalent registration evidence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC or source-of-funds questions, correct ownership charts, and resubmit missing documents. If a bank declines onboarding, seek another authorized deposit institution or use a French notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-notice publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish an avis de constitution in an authorized journal of legal notices or approved online legal-notice service before filing. The notice must state the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, President identity, and registration details required by applicable rules. Retain the publication certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice if the journal, department, legal form, corporate name, capital, address, or officer information is incorrect. Attach the corrected certificate to the filing or registry response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online declaration of creation, upload the signed articles, capital-deposit certificate, legal-notice certificate, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, identity documents, and beneficial-owner information. Identify each natural person ultimately owning or controlling the company; if no individual meets the ownership or control tests, identify the legally determined senior managing officer. Pay any applicable administrative or beneficial-owner charges shown by the portal.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder documents and French translations, if applicable
Filing power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard and answer deficiency notices within the stated deadline. Upload corrected documents through the portal, preserve the filing receipt, and escalate unresolved registry issues to the competent Greffe or INPI support channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration activation and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI, French tax administration, URSSAF, commercial bank, and applicable local authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the SIREN/SIRET and Kbis or registration extract, release or convert the capital account, open the operating bank account, activate VAT and corporate-tax accounts as applicable, register employees with URSSAF before hiring, maintain the share register and decisions register, and implement accounting, invoice, consumer, product-safety, and intellectual-property controls.
required_dossiers: Final articles and corporate decisions register
URSSAF employer-registration data, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax, bank, or social-security registration discrepancies using the registration extract and filing receipt. Update the INPI record promptly after changes to officers, address, activity, ownership, or beneficial ownership.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent Préfecture of the establishment location, generally supported by the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL). There is no general French manufacturing licence for ordinary costume, apparel, prop, or synthetic-wig production.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating licence; where the premises fall within the classified installations regime, an ICPE declaration (déclaration ICPE), registration (enregistrement ICPE), or environmental authorization (autorisation environnementale) may be required under the French Environmental Code.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Préfecture and DREAL, with the competent environmental authority, including the applicable Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale (MRAe), for environmental-assessment opinions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a formal EIA for low-volume tailoring, apparel assembly, prop finishing, and wig production without significant combustion, solvent use, chemical treatment, or wastewater discharge. A case-specific screening is required where ICPE nomenclature thresholds are met; projects subject to environmental authorization may require a full environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE prescriptions and French Environmental Code requirements. Obtain authorization or agreement for industrial wastewater discharge where required; prevent discharge of dyes, adhesives, solvents, or contaminated rinse water to public sewers without approval. Control VOC emissions from solvents, paints, coatings, and adhesives under applicable ICPE and product-use rules. Segregate hazardous waste, maintain required waste traceability through Trackdéchets where applicable, and use authorized waste contractors. Exact thresholds depend on equipment capacity, stored quantities, substances, and site classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain premises and fire-safety compliance appropriate to the building classification. If customers or the public enter the premises, comply with Établissement recevant du public (ERP) rules and obtain any required opening or accessibility authorization from the commune and its safety/accessibility commission, with the Service départemental d'incendie et de secours (SDIS) involved as applicable. Verify structural load, electrical installations, machinery guarding, emergency exits, ventilation, chemical storage, and workplace risk controls. There is no general occupational operating clearance; the employer must complete occupational-risk assessment, maintain a DUERP, arrange occupational-health services, and comply with Labour Code inspection requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for the registered office; non-residents: Pôle TVA des non-résidents (Noisy-le-Grand); official portals: impots.gouv.fr, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (INPI Guichet Unique), portail-facturation.gouv.fr (PPF).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Established SAS: (1) file incorporation at the INPI Guichet Unique, obtaining RCS registration and INSEE SIREN/SIRET; (2) DGFiP allocates the intra-community TVA number (FR+11 characters) after INSEE notification to the SIE; (3) open the tax account at the competent SIE and select the VAT regime (normal or simplified real); (4) obtain an EORI customs number via DGFiP/customs (needed for all export declarations) and register for the DEB/EC Sales List scheme. Foreign non-established entity: file a direct VAT-registration application with the Pôle TVA des non-résidents before the first French taxable supply; non-EU entities must in addition appoint a DGFiP-approved tax representative (Article 289 A CGI) jointly and severally liable for VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists in France: an SAS is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (Article 206(1) CGI) on its worldwide profit (subject to PE/asset attribution and treaty relief, e.g., US-France DTA arts. 5/7). Available elections: (i) group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale, Article 223 A CGI) for ≥95%-owned French subsidiaries; (ii) single VAT group (assujetti unique, Article 256 C-II CGI) subject to DGFiP approval; (iii) option for the simplified real VAT regime (régime simplifié réel), including semi-annual instalments; (iv) renunciation/option of the franchise en base (small-business VAT exemption) — applicable only to small taxpayers; mandatory to recover input VAT; (v) option to tax immovable property leases. Election to be taxed as a pass-through is unavailable to an SAS.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (prudential supervision delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution – ACPR; exchange control administration under the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques and Banque de France for statistical Balance of Payments reporting)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account operations. France applies EU Treaty provisions (TFEU Articles 63–66) guaranteeing free movement of capital and unrestricted profit remittance. No prior approval is required for dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital repatriation to shareholders in EU or non-EU jurisdictions, provided the underlying transactions are bona fide and supported by standard accounting documentation. Capital contributions (equity or shareholder loans) must be reported via the Banque de France's mandatory 'Lettre de déclaration de transaction financière' (Annexe 1 / Form CRM) for statistical purposes only when the transaction exceeds the reporting threshold (currently €15,000 per transaction for monetary movements with non-residents). Withholding tax at 25% (at source) applies to dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders absent a tax treaty (rates may be reduced under the France–[Country] DTA and under Paired Parent-Subsidiary Directive). No currency inconvertibility risk or local FX rationing exists; the EUR is a free-floating reserve currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds and no statutory timeline for repatriation. Exporters may retain full receipts in EUR or hold foreign-currency accounts with any authorized EU/EEA credit institution. Invoice settlement can be made under open account, advance payment, or documentary collection terms. The only residual obligation is indirect: proceeds received from non-EU customers that are paid via SWIFT to a French bank account must be properly classified with a Balance of Payments (BOP) purpose code for national statistics, and the enterprise must maintain records for ACPR/TRACFIN anti-money laundering scrutiny. No conversion ratio applies; the enterprise may freely choose to convert or hold foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) + Dedicated USD/EUR Sweep Account for FX
Operational Account + Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) for equity injection
Operational Account with SEPA and international remittance module
Operational Account + Trade Finance Facility (for commercial LC issuance)
Operational Account with dedicated merchant acquiring settlement account
Multi-currency Operational Account (EUR, USD, CNY) and Cross-Border Liquidity Hub

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for operational/non-credit payment flows; Medium for core treasury banking. French-regulated EMIs (Qonto, Shine, Lydia) and EU-passporting EMIs (Revolut Business, Wise Business, N26 Business, BNP's specialized neobanks) may open accounts under the PSD2 licensing regime with fully remote KYC video verification. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs cannot grant credit or offer commercial loan facilities without a separate credit institution license; (ii) salary payments must be made through an account that supports SEPA Direct Debit and Instant SEPA Credit; (iii) certain merchant acquiring mandates (e.g., direct acquiring for Shopify Payments) may require settlement into a bank account held at a licensed credit institution rather than an EMI; (iv) TRACFIN reporting duties and UBO verification are identical to traditional banks; (v) French corporate tax administration (DGFiP) aligns anti-fraud identifiers to the EMI's KYC record; (vi) EMIs offering only virtual IBANs may trigger enhanced scrutiny under ACPR guidance on 'virtual IBAN' transactional opacity. Recommended structure: maintain a traditional Tier-1 bank account as the principal treasury anchor and use an EMI as a secondary collection/payout rail for merchant settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence: Yes for most traditional French banks for the initial client acceptance interview of the legal representative (Président / Directeur Général) and any natural-person beneficial owners (typically the direct and indirect shareholders holding >25% plus the Signatories). A physical branch rendez-vous at the commercial branch is standard for BNP, SG, CA, and BPCE; remote video onboarding is permitted under AMLD5/PSD2 and ACPR guidance, but is accepted primarily by digital banks, EMIs, and some niche account packages of traditional banks (e.g., SG's 'Orange Bank' successor offers fully remote). For the SAS structure, the following will be required at interview: (i) the legal representative's original passport or national ID; (ii) proof of residential address (dated utility bill or tax assessment); (iii) corporate K-bis extract (≤3 months old); (iv) Articles of Association; (v) UBO declaration form (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs – DBE) as filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; (vi) list of authorised signatories. Remote opening is permissible if the bank uses a certified video-identification provider compliant with ACPR's position on digital onboarding; a remote documentary-only opening (without video interview) is generally rejected for non-resident owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO discrepancy / undisclosed indirect ownership by non-EU persons (e.g., a Chinese resident holding >25% through a nominee trust)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain of ownership certificates, notarised UBO declaration (form DBE), shareholder register (registre des mouvements de titres), trust deed or nominee agreement, sworn English/French translations, passports of each UBO, and a written explanation of source-of-funds for initial capital

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency B2C card settlement volatility (Stripe/Shopify Payments deposits) flagged as unexpected transaction patterns vs declared turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month TFW (taxe sur les salaires) and VAT returns (CA3) proving declared revenue, merchant processor settlement reports, e-commerce platform sales logs, refund/dispute registers, PCI-DSS compliance attestation, and a board-approved treasury policy confirming concentration risk and cash-flow denominators

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to licensed IP proprietors (theatrical costume licenses, e.g., film/TV studios) triggering IP-rights and OFAC/FSU (US Treasury) country-screening alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed license agreements, royalty statements, licensor's standing and registration documents, FTP/TFTS due diligence file confirming no sanctioned counterparty, export classification of the licensed goods under US EAR (if applicable), and a compliance memo confirming absence of revenue split to design-industry controlled entities

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large upfront capital injection from an offshore holding company (e.g., the SAS receiving >€500k equity contribution from a Hong Kong or Singapore affiliate) triggering 'shell-bank' suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equity subscription agreement or memorandum of investment, board resolutions of both entities, audited financial statements of the investing entity, source-of-funds corroboration (bank statements, sale agreements, dividend vouchers), regulatory capital adequacy memo, and an ACPR-compliant source-of-wealth questionnaire

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual rapid turnover in synthetic-wig and costume trade with ambiguous customs descriptions (dual-use or counterfeit exposure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Import/export customs declarations (DAU/SAD), CE conformity and textile register certificates for fibre classification, trademark licensee approvals, fabric composition laboratory reports, and letter of compliance from customs broker confirming correct HS codes (HS 6504/6117)

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (i) Shareholder funds transfer via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) to the SAS's EUR IBAN at the French Tier-1 bank; (ii) the MT103 must carry a BOP purpose code consistent with OECD/Eurostat Balance of Payments classification – for equity injection, use code 'SD' or the Banque de France statistical code 'P400' (equity capital) or, for shareholder loans, 'P300' (loans) with the 6-digit BOP code '71000' (direct investment equity); (iii) a formal capital increase must be executed notarially and filed with the Greffe within the statutory timeframe; (iv) the bank will request a copy of the 'Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs' and a statement confirming no sanction-listed counterparties; (v) if the injected amount exceeds €15,000, the Banque de France's mandatory statistical declaration (Form CRM – 'Déclaration de change') must be filed electronically within 30 days of the transaction. Hedge-linked inflows (e.g., prepayment of export receivables) should be routed under code '80000/88000'. Verification: the bank's compliance unit will require a copy of the subscription agreement, board minutes, and evidence of tax residence of the investing entity (tax certificate) for CRS/FATCA reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (instant or standard) for EUR-denominated supplier payments within the EU/EEA (free up to €50,000, 1 business day settlement); (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR international transfers to suppliers in China/Hong Kong/US (advices must include the correct purpose code '300' – goods trade, commercial invoice reference, and Incoterm; typical cost €10–€50 per transfer with settlement T+1 to T+2); (iii) Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP600) for large procurement contracts of synthetic fabrics, wigs, and accessory components from non-OECD suppliers (typically issued by the French bank as L/C at sight or 90 days; requires a dedicated trade finance sub-limit and underlying proforma invoice); (iv) Standby LC or bank guarantee for licensing-secured purchase obligations (rarely needed for the low-risk standard tier); (v) Merchant settlement outflows: Stripe and Shopify Payments (via Stripe Connect) remit net card settlement proceeds to the French IBAN in EUR using SEPA Credit; if the platforms are configured in USD, the merchant must hold a USD concentration account to avoid conversion at the platform level. All outbound payments to non-EU beneficiaries must be flagged with the proper BOP code in the MT103/MT103FIELDS (Field 33B, 51A, 52A, 57A, 70/72) and should match the underlying commercial invoice to pass TRACFIN monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Outright Forward (standard deliverable forward with Banque de France-recognised ISDA/EMIR collateral; a corporate 'confirm' is sufficient for plain vanilla trades)
EUR/CNY deliverable FX forward (onshore CNY forwards are deliverable to the extent the counterparty is a licensed Chinese bank; otherwise use non-deliverable back-to-back with two offsetting legs)
Rolling forward window contracts (for merchant settlement volatility)
FX swaps (short-term liquidity matching between EUR and USD/CNY accounts)
Cross-currency swap (for long-term capital injection hedging, maturity aligned to the capital injection schedule)
European-style barrier options and call/put options in EUR/USD (subject to ACPR MiFID-licensed counterparty trading capacity and board-approved treasury mandate; not available on EMI platforms)

NDFs are permissible for exotic pairs where the EUR leg is fully convertible; however, EUR/USD and EUR/CNY are both deliverable for FR-resident entities, so NDFs are generally unavailable and unnecessary for standard trade flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; approval by the shareholders or sole shareholder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A director may be ordered to convene the shareholders and may incur civil or criminal liability; failure to approve does not itself trigger automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) for filing in the National Register of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president of the court may issue an injunction to file, potentially subject to a penalty payment. Continued non-compliance can lead to court-ordered measures; there is no automatic strike-off solely for a late accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a year ending on 31 December, by the second working day after 1 May, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges generally start at 10% and may rise to 40% after a formal notice and 80% in specified cases, in addition to late-payment interest. No automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payment of the Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 15 December; advance-payment obligations depend on the prior-year assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest. CFE is a tax assessment, not an annual company-renewal filing; no automatic strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional requirements may apply to parent companies and groups under control or significant-influence rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the Plan comptable général (PCG); IFRS is not generally mandatory for standalone statutory accounts of an unlisted SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation. The company must keep its beneficial-ownership information accurate and file an update with the National Register of Companies within 30 days of a change. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's securities movement register and shareholder accounts; the articles of association may impose additional formalities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholders' meeting and sole-shareholder decision minutes
Securities movement register and individual shareholder accounts
Accounting books and supporting records required under French law

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 330-1,650 per year; provider, location, and service scope dependent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,300-11,000 per year when a statutory audit is required; scope and company complexity dependent

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat standard French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, 'IS') under Article 219 CGI. A reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per 12-month period for companies with net turnover strictly below EUR 10 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 42,500 tranche; research tax credit (CIR) at 33.33% of eligible R&D expenditures up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that; intellectual property 'box' regime taxing qualifying patent/innovation royalty income at 10%; 'jeune entreprise innovante' (JEI) social and corporate tax exemptions; tax loss carryback (report en arrière) of up to EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats) with annexes 2050-2058-G, filed electronically via the DGFiP TDFC/EFI tele-procedure on impots.gouv.fr (or via EDI partner software). Dividend distributions are declared on Form 2561 and related withholding tax remitted on Form 2777.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate income tax is discharged through four quarterly instalments (Forms 2571-SD/2572-SD) due 15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with a final balancing payment on filing the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return must be filed by the second working day after 1 May (e.g., 6 May 2024). For fiscal years not ending on 31 December, the return is due within three months of the fiscal year-end. Instalment payments fall due on the 15th of the respective months unless the tax liability is below EUR 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity, SIREN number, legal form, address, activity code (APE 3240Z), and shareholding structure as at the closing date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate for foreign shareholders their country of residence, percentage of capital, and any dividend distribution mandate; no French fiscal representative is required for a French SAS merely because its shareholders are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary balance sheet: stated assets, liabilities, share capital, loans from partners and pre-tax accounting equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loans granted by non-resident shareholders must be disclosed separately as related-party debts; arm's-length interest and thin capitalisation ceilings (Art. 212 CGI) will be verified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines BA / BB – Net book result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit (BA) or net loss (BB) for the fiscal year before fiscal reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same entries for a non-resident-owned SAS; foreign management fees, royalties and re-invoiced costs must be supported by service contracts and substantiated benefit tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after reintegration of non-deductible charges and after allocation of deductible items, including base for the split between the 15% reduced rate and the 25% standard rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reject non-deductible withholding taxes borne for foreign shareholders; verify transfer pricing adjustments on imports of cosplay apparel and re-invoiced prototyping costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intra-form split of taxable profit: first EUR 42,500 at 15% (line 330); remaining balance at 25% (line 331).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% reduced rate is available to the French SAS regardless of foreign ownership, provided the EUR 10 million turnover threshold is met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward: deductible during each of the next five fiscal years, limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above that threshold in each year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No distinction for non-resident ownership; change of business activity or acquisition of the SAS may block the carry-forward under loss-trafficking rules (Art. 209 CGI).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of tax credits (CIR, CICE legacy, innovation tax credit) against gross corporate income tax; excess credits are refundable after 3 years or immediately for eligible young companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The research credit remains available to the French SAS even if the cosplay manufacturing R&D is partly subcontracted to a foreign related party; the subcontractor must be arm's-length-priced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares dividends decided by the sole shareholder/board, identifies each beneficiary, and computes the applicable withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporate shareholder, the French SAS must apply the 25% withholding tax unless a treaty claim (Form 5000 plus residence certificate) is validly received before payment; EU parent companies holding 5% or more for 2 years may qualify for the 0% mère-fille exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return triggers a 10% surcharge if filed within 30 days of the statutory deadline, 40% if filed later, and 80% in the case of abuse of law or fraudulent manoeuvres (Art. 1728 CGI); a 5% penalty applies for non-electronic filing; late payment interest runs at 0.20% per calendar month (Art. 1727 CGI). Failure to file within 30 days after a formal notice exposes the company to ex officio assessment (taxation d'office) with enhanced interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 119-2 CGI; distributions to French-individual residents are subject to the 30% flat tax (PFU). The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, transposed through the French mère-fille regime, provides a 0% withholding exemption where the EU parent holds at least 5% of the capital for at least 2 years; non-EU treaty shareholders may claim reduced rates (commonly 15% general or 5% for substantial holdings, e.g., France-US treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must complete French Form 5000 (or 5001 for individuals), have it certified by the tax authority of the country of residence, and combine it with the official residence certificate (TRC) and a certificate of shareholding/beneficial ownership. These documents must reach the French paying company before the distribution so that the reduced treaty rate is applied at source; where tax has been over-withheld, the refund claim is filed with the DGFiP service of the paying company within the statutory limitation period (generally 31 December of the second year following the tax year). The beneficial owner must be able to prove substance and not be a conduit company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties/industrial property rights: France levies a 33.33% withholding tax on patents, patentable inventions, manufacturing processes and similar IP royalties paid by a French debtor to non-residents without a French permanent establishment (Art. 182 B bis CGI). Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive the rate is 0% for EU associated companies; most French treaties reduce it to 5% or 0% (forms 5000 + TRC required). Interest on trade loans and banking debt paid to non-resident creditors is generally exempt from French withholding tax at the statutory level; however, interest paid to shareholders in non-cooperative jurisdictions (ETNC) is subject to punitive 50% or 75% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A French SAS must prepare full Master File and Local File where its annual net turnover or gross balance-sheet assets exceed EUR 400,000,000, or where it is owned at least 50% (directly or indirectly) by a non-resident entity meeting the same threshold (Art. L. 13 AA LPF). Simplified transfer pricing documentation is triggered from EUR 50,000,000 annual turnover (Art. L. 13 AB LPF). Country-by-country reporting applies to groups of French resident entities with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a standalone ESR regime in the Gulf/Cayman sense. Instead, substance is legally enforced through: (i) the abuse-of-law doctrine (abus de droit, Art. L.64 LPF) for artificial structures; (ii) the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test embedded in applicable tax treaties, denying treaty benefits where one of the principal purposes is treaty shopping; (iii) the EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules (Art. 212 bis CGI); and (iv) the requirement of a genuine French permanent establishment. A hollow French SAS interposed in the cosplay retail supply chain solely to access French tax advantages or treaty rates can be disregarded, repriced, and penalised at 80%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of taxable revenue, concealment of profits, fictitious deductions, false invoices in the cosplay apparel import-manufacturing chain, or organised deception of the tax authorities (Art. 1741 CGI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; aggravated fraud raises the penalties to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years. Tax reassessment is increased by 80% and the judgment may be published in the press at the offender's cost.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS president and de facto directors who participate in the fraud are personally prosecuted; sanctions include criminal fines, travel bans, freezing of personal assets, prohibition from managing a business, and loss of tax compliance integrity for future licensing or public procurement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Wrongful Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-filing of Form 2065-SD, late filing beyond 30 days after notice, refusal to provide accounting records, or knowingly filing an incomplete balance-sheet declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of 10% (within 30 days), 40% (after 30 days), or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvre; monthly late interest of 0.20%; ex officio assessment (taxation d'office) without opportunity to dispute the tax base; automatic tax levy without prior declaratory right.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is personally and severally liable for penalties and withholding tax that was not paid over where the default results from his or her deliberate misconduct (Art. L.267 LPF), and may be subject to commercial court disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishment or maintenance of a French SAS without economic substance, staff or local decision-making, created artificially to obtain treaty benefits, avoid 25% dividend withholding, or access CIR refunds and the 15% reduced rate without genuine business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse of law procedure (Art. L.64 LPF) entailing restitution of the avoided tax, 80% penalty, interest at 0.20% per month, and possible rejection of treaty claims under the Principal Purpose Test; the arrangement may be recharacterised as a conduit disregarded for French tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or implemented the artificial scheme are jointly and severally liable for the reassessed tax, penalties and interest; in severe cases they face fraud charges, corporate disqualification, and a ban from holding office in French regulated entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or present the Master File, Local File or simplified documentation on request; neglect of arm's-length benchmarking for intercompany purchases of cosplay costumes, character licensed IP royalties, or management fees; unjustified transfer mispricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of EUR 150,000 for non-communication of transfer pricing documentation (Art. 1735 ter B CGI); incomplete documents attract fines of EUR 15,000 per item; the tax authority may reprice the transactions and assert withholding tax deficiencies on recharacterised distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Mangers who knowingly sign TP documentation containing false valuations are exposed to personal prosecution for fraud; the company's tax debt can be recovered from directors under Art. L.267 LPF where non-filing or concealment is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering of Tax Fraud / AML Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Converting, transferring, or concealing the proceeds of tax evasion, including routing cosplay-related e-commerce profits (Stripe or Shopify Payments proceeds) through opaque foreign shell accounts, or engaging in habitual laundering of tax-fraud proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 750,000 and imprisonment of up to 10 years for aggravated money laundering (Art. 324-2 Criminal Code); additional confiscation of the laundered assets, closure of the business, and publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director and beneficial owner face personal travel bans, seizure of bank accounts and real property, freezing of shares, and a commercial ban; the corporate veil is pierced under the theory of independent fault (faute détachable) committed by the manager for the aggregate amount of laundered funds.
